title: He was right.
paragraphs: He was right.
That’s what makes it terrifying.
Ahithophel did not give foolish advice. He gave perfect counsel—sharp, immediate, decisive. Strike now. Catch David while he is weak. End it in one blow (2 Samuel 17:1–3).

It was clean.
Strategic.
Brilliant.
And God broke it.
Pause there.
Because some of you think if your plan is smart enough, if your timing is precise enough, if your influence is strong enough—then it will stand.
But Scripture says otherwise.
“The Lord had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel…” (2 Samuel 17:14).
Read that again.

Not bad counsel.
Not flawed thinking.
Good counsel.
And God still shattered it.
Ahithophel was respected like a living oracle. When he spoke, kings leaned in. Armies moved. Futures shifted (2 Samuel 16:23). This man understood power, timing, pressure.
But he made one fatal mistake.
He aligned his brilliance against the will of God.
And when Absalom rejected his plan in favor of Hushai’s slower, weaker strategy, Ahithophel saw it instantly.
It’s over.

The rebellion will fall.
The king will return.
Judgment is coming.
He read the moment perfectly.
But instead of repenting…
He went home.
Set his house in order.
And hanged himself (2 Samuel 17:23).
Let that sink in.
A man can be wise enough to read the future…
…and still be blind to grace.
This is not just history. This is a mirror.
Because some of you are Ahithophel in a suit.

You know how to win arguments.
You know how to position yourself.
You know how to make moves that impress people.
But deep down, you are resisting God.
And when your plan collapses, your instinct is not repentance—
…it’s control, withdrawal, or despair.
Listen to me.
Broken plans are not always failure. Sometimes they are mercy.
God did not just defeat Ahithophel’s counsel to save David.

He did it to preserve His redemptive story—
the line that would lead to Jesus Christ, the true and better King.
If Ahithophel’s plan had succeeded, David would have been destroyed.
And if David falls, the promise trembles.
But God guards His promise with unstoppable sovereignty.
Even over “good” advice.
And then the story whispers something deeper.
It echoes forward.
Another man.
Another betrayal.
Another hanging.
Ahithophel betrayed David—the anointed king—and died in despair.
Judas betrayed Jesus—the greater Son of David—and also died in despair (Matthew 27:5).
Do you see it?
The Bible is not random. It is revealing.

Two men.
Two betrayals.
Two endings soaked in regret.
But here’s the dividing line:
Despair is not the only door.

Judas ran from Jesus.
Ahithophel never turned back.
But Peter—who also failed, who also denied—ran toward Jesus and found restoration (John 21).
That is the Gospel.
Not that you won’t fail.
But that Jesus receives those who return.
So here’s the question that will not leave you alone tonight:

When God overturns your plan…
when your strategy collapses…
when the door you were sure about slams shut—
What will you do?
Will you tighten your grip?
Will you protect your pride?
Will you spiral into silent despair?
Or will you bow?
Repent.
And trust that God is doing something better than your best idea ever could?
Because let’s be honest.
Some of you are frustrated right now.

You prayed.
You planned.
You executed.
And it still fell apart.
What if that collapse was not rejection—
…but protection?
What if God saw where that path would lead…
…and loved you enough to destroy it?
Ahithophel teaches us this with painful clarity:
Wisdom without surrender leads to ruin.
You can be right—and still be wrong before God.
You can be brilliant—and still be broken.
You can be admired—and still be lost.
But in Christ—
There is another ending.
Jesus is the King Ahithophel rejected.
Jesus is the Savior Judas betrayed.
And Jesus is still the Redeemer who looks at failures, traitors, and prideful hearts—
…and says, “Come back.”
Not tomorrow.
Now.
So don’t waste your collapse.
Don’t numb it.
Don’t spin it.
Let it humble you.
Let it strip the illusion that you are in control.
Let it drive you to the feet of the One whose plans never fail.
Because the same God who defeated Ahithophel’s counsel…
…is the same God who sent His Son to save sinners like you and me.
And at the cross, human wisdom tried its best again.
Plotting. Scheming. Killing the Son of God.
And once again—
God overturned it.
What looked like defeat became salvation.
What looked like the end became eternal life.
This is your invitation.

Lay down your pride.
Release your plans.
Run to Christ.
Because His mercy is greater than your mistakes.
His grace is deeper than your despair.
And His purpose will stand—whether you fight it or fall into it.
Choose surrender.
Choose life.
Choose Jesus.
“For the Lord had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel…” (2 Samuel 17:14)
And in that defeat…
He was writing a greater victory.
